precepts.text: In that day the Lord with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea. Remember it says the dragon fought and his angels. He is going to punish leviathan, the piercing serpent. That is the white man. And he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea. That is America.
precepts.point: And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him. Who deceived the world is not just a spiritual demon. This is his children. The white man, Edom, Lucifer, that transformed himself into an angel of light.
precepts.why:
Daniel said, “And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered.” That time is Armageddon, when all nations rise up and fight, and Michael rises up to fight for us. Revelation 12 is the same thing: “And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon.” It's not talking about war in the sky, as Christians say, Lucifer fighting with God and his angels. It's all nations fighting with each other. This is the time of trouble.

“and the dragon fought and his angels.” Who is the dragon? Lucifer: America and Europe. His angels are his armies. Isaiah proves it: “In that day the Lord with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.”

Leviathan, the piercing serpent, that crooked serpent, is the white man. And the dragon that is in the sea is America. The Lord will punish him with his great and strong sword in that day, the same day Michael stands up for Daniel's people and they are delivered.

precepts.text: The Lord gathers one by one all ye children of Israel, and they come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria and the outcasts in the land of Egypt: that is who Egypt my people is.
precepts.point: Blessed be Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands: the one verse they might run to for another nation, and a few chapters on the Lord beats off from the stream of Egypt and gathers one by one the children of Israel, those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt, to worship at Jerusalem. My people in Egypt and Assyria means Israel in those lands, the remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar and Hamath, Judah and Joseph brought again out of Egypt and Assyria.

precepts.why:
“Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.” That is the one verse they might run with: see, Egypt is his people and Assyria is his people, so the Egyptians and the Assyrians are saved too. No problem. Go over a few chapters and see where this Egypt and Assyria are.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.” Gathered one by one: who? The children of Israel.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown”: that is Christ coming. “And they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt.” Earlier it said Egypt and Assyria; here it is the land of Assyria and the land of Egypt, and the ones coming out of them are the children of Israel. So who is “Egypt my people” and Assyria? Israelites.

“And shall worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem.” My people in Egypt and my people in Assyria means Israel in those lands, scattered there and gathered out one by one to worship at Jerusalem. That is how precepts work: you don't build a doctrine for another nation on one verse.
